chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon them) who said:
Temporary marriage (Mut'ah) is a marriage with inheritance and a marriage without inheritance. If inheritance is stipulated, it exists; if it is not stipulated, it does not exist.
ai.seo_question: Does temporary marriage (Mut'ah) automatically include inheritance rights in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates that the inheritance right in temporary marriage (Mut'ah) is not automatic but strictly contingent upon explicit stipulation (shart) within the contract. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence, allowing parties to customize the legal consequences of the union, thereby distinguishing Mut'ah from permanent marriage where inheritance is inherent. This principle highlights the contractual nature of the bond, where specific rights are activated only by mutual agreement.
